data: Pinpoint lunar landing; toppled but operational
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

JAXA’s 2024 lunar lander. Touched down within 100 m of its target — pinpoint accuracy unprecedented for a lunar lander — but landed on its nose at roughly 90 degrees, with solar panels facing away from the Sun. Still operated and survived four lunar nights without radioisotope heating — a record for passively-heated lunar surface missions.
First precision landing within 100 m of target on another world
First U.S. lunar landing since Apollo; sideways
First-ever lunar far-side sample return. Apollo basin landing 2024-06-01 (UTC); 1935 g returned to Inner Mongolia 2024-06-25
Blue Origin's first-generation lunar cargo lander — single-stage hydrogen / oxygen vehicle, ~3 t to the surface
Japan's first private Moon landing attempts; Mission 1 (2023) and Mission 2 (2025) both crashed
First landing near the lunar south pole

Japan's Smart Lander demonstrated pinpoint precision landing — targeting within 100 m accuracy vs the km-scale standard of all previous missions. Landed nose-down at roughly 90° from the intended attitude, leaving its solar panels initially pointing away from the Sun; operations resumed nine days later once the Sun angle shifted. Japan became the fifth nation to achieve a lunar soft landing.
